title: Chicken Marsala
subtitle: Pan-fried chicken in a mushroom and wine-style sauce
excerpt: The sauce here is built from chicken stock and a splash of mirin in place of Marsala wine, which gives sweetness and colour without the need for a fortified wine. Flattening the chicken breasts first means they cook through quickly and stay juicy.
sourceNotes: Chicken Marsala is a staple of Italian-American restaurants, derived from the Sicilian practice of cooking veal in Marsala wine. The dish became popular in the United States in the twentieth century, often appearing in the same diners that made chicken parmigiana famous.

content.text: Dust the chicken in flour just before it hits the pan -- if you flour it too early, the coating becomes sticky and does not crisp. Work in two batches if your pan is not large enough to keep the chicken in a single layer.
Flatten the chicken breasts between sheets of baking paper or cling film to about 1 cm. Season and dust lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat 1 tbsp of butter and the olive oil in the frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Add another 1 tbsp of butter to the pan. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook without stirring for 3 minutes until golden. Stir and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Add the chicken stock and mirin, scraping up any browned bits from the base of the pan. Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce has reduced by a third.
Stir in the remaining butter and return the chicken to the pan. Spoon the sauce over the top and cook for 1 minute to heat through. Scatter with parsley and serve.

items.fix: Remove the chicken and simmer the sauce alone for another 3-4 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon.

items.cause: Cooked too long in the first stage.
items.fix: Flatten the breasts more evenly next time and pull them from the pan as soon as they are just cooked through -- they will finish in the sauce.
